name: Servers and infrastructure
description: Linux, web servers, Docker, backups, SSL, deploys, health checks.

cards.subject: The root user
says: has user ID 0 and unrestricted control of the system
bypasses the normal file permission checks
cards.use: want to explain why daily work should not run under the all-powerful account
not: is limited by the same file permissions as ordinary users

cards.subject: The sudo command
says: runs a single command with another user's privileges, usually root
is governed by a sudoers policy
can record which user ran which command
cards.use: need one administrative command without staying logged in as root
not: permanently turns the whole session into the root user

cards.subject: A file mode
says: is shown as read, write and execute bits for owner, group and others
can be written as an octal number such as 640
is changed with chmod
cards.use: need to stop other users reading a file
not: is stored inside the file's name

cards.subject: A symbolic link
says: is a file that holds the path of another file
breaks when its target is moved or deleted
is how an enabled Apache site normally points at its available config
cards.use: want one file to appear at a second path without copying it
not: is an independent full copy of its target

cards.subject: Log rotation
says: renames and compresses old log files on a schedule
deletes the oldest logs after a set number of rotations
is commonly handled by logrotate
cards.use: need logs to stop filling the disk
not: makes a log file larger so more history fits in it

cards.subject: A cron job
says: runs a command on a repeating time schedule
is defined by five time fields followed by the command
runs with a minimal environment, so absolute paths are safest
cards.use: need a backup to run every night without anyone remembering
not: runs only while a user is logged in

cards.subject: Load average
says: counts processes running or waiting to run, averaged over 1, 5 and 15 minutes
has to be read against the number of CPU cores
cards.use: need to judge whether a busy server is saturated on CPU
not: is the percentage of RAM currently in use

cards.subject: An inode
says: stores a file's owner, permissions and data location but not its name
exists in a limited number per filesystem
can run out while free space remains
cards.use: see 'No space left on device' although df shows free space
not: is a block of RAM reserved for one running process

cards.subject: The OOM killer
says: is a kernel mechanism that ends a process when memory runs out
chooses its victim by a score based on memory use
leaves a message in the kernel log
cards.use: need to find out why a service vanished with no error of its own
not: compresses memory pages so that no process ever has to end

cards.subject: The df command
says: reports used and free space for each mounted filesystem
is the usual first check when a disk is suspected full
cards.use: need to see whether the disk is full
not: lists which folder uses the most space

cards.subject: The du command
says: adds up the space used by directories and files
finds the heavy folder when run with a depth limit
cards.use: need to find which folder is eating the disk
not: shows free space for each filesystem

cards.subject: The free command
says: shows used, free and cached memory
reports swap usage alongside RAM
cards.use: need to check whether the server is short of memory
not: reports disk space on each filesystem

cards.subject: The top command
says: shows a live, refreshing list of processes, by default sorted by CPU use
displays the load average in its header
cards.use: need to see which process is using the CPU right now
not: prints one snapshot and exits

cards.subject: The ss command
says: lists listening and connected sockets
shows the owning process with the -p option when run with enough privilege
cards.use: need to see which process is listening on a port
not: lists every file a process has open, regular files included

cards.subject: The lsof command
says: lists open files, including sockets, for each process
can reveal a deleted file that a process still holds open
cards.use: need to find what keeps disk space used after a log file was deleted
not: lists only the TCP ports in the listening state

cards.subject: The journalctl command
says: reads logs from the systemd journal
filters to one service with the -u option
can show only entries since a given time
cards.use: need the recent logs of a systemd service
not: rotates the log files under /var/log

cards.subject: The tail -f command
says: follows a file and prints new lines as they are appended
is the quick way to watch a log while requests arrive
cards.use: need to watch a log live
not: deletes the oldest lines from a file

cards.subject: The rsync command
says: copies only the differences between source and destination
removes files missing from the source when given --delete
uses a delta algorithm so unchanged parts of files are not re-sent
cards.use: need to mirror a directory to a server efficiently
not: re-sends every file in full on each run

cards.subject: The curl command
says: makes an HTTP request from the command line
shows only the response headers with -I
can print just the status code when given -w with the http_code variable
cards.use: need to test a URL's status code without a browser
not: edits the web server's configuration

cards.subject: A reverse proxy
says: accepts client requests and forwards them to a backend server
hides the backend's address from clients
can terminate TLS on behalf of the backend
cards.use: need public traffic to reach an app that listens only on localhost
not: sits on the user's side and fetches pages on their behalf

cards.subject: An Apache virtual host
says: is declared in Apache with a VirtualHost block
lets one Apache install serve several sites chosen by hostname and port
cards.use: need two domains served from one Apache install
not: is declared with a server block containing listen and server_name

cards.subject: An Nginx server block
says: is declared with a server block containing listen and server_name
selects the site to serve by matching server_name
cards.use: need two domains served from one Nginx install
not: is declared in Apache with a VirtualHost element

cards.subject: The ProxyPass directive
says: maps a URL path to a backend address in Apache
needs the Apache proxy modules enabled
is paired with ProxyPassReverse so that redirects from the backend are rewritten
cards.use: need Apache to forward the whole site to a local app
not: passes the original Host header on to the backend

cards.subject: The ProxyPreserveHost directive
says: passes the original Host header on to the backend
stops the backend seeing its own address as the requested host
cards.use: need the app behind Apache to see the public hostname
not: chooses which backend receives the request

cards.subject: An .htaccess file
says: holds per-directory Apache settings
is honoured only where AllowOverride permits it
is re-read on every request, unlike the main config
cards.use: need per-directory rules on a host where you cannot edit the main config
not: is read once when Apache starts

cards.subject: The prefork MPM
says: uses a separate single-threaded process for each connection
suits code that is not thread-safe, such as classic mod_php
cards.use: need an Apache processing model for non-thread-safe modules
not: hands idle keep-alive connections off to a shared helper thread

cards.subject: The event MPM
says: hands idle keep-alive connections off so they do not tie up a worker thread
is a threaded Apache processing model
cards.use: want Apache to hold many idle keep-alive connections cheaply
not: uses one single-threaded process for every connection

cards.subject: A 301 response
says: tells clients a URL has moved permanently
may be cached by browsers for a long time
cards.use: need to send http traffic to https for good
not: marks a move as temporary and expects clients to keep the old URL

cards.subject: A 302 response
says: tells clients a move is temporary
expects clients to keep using the original URL next time
cards.use: need to send visitors elsewhere for now, such as during a trial
not: tells search engines the page has permanently moved

cards.subject: A 403 response
says: means the server understood the request and refuses it
is what an IP access rule returns to an address that is not allowed
cards.use: need to explain why a blocked address gets a refusal rather than a missing page
not: means the page does not exist

cards.subject: A 502 response
says: means the proxy received an invalid reply or none from the backend
is typical when the app behind the proxy has crashed or stopped
cards.use: see the proxy answer instantly with an error because the app is down
not: means the proxy waited too long for the backend

cards.subject: A 503 response
says: means the service is temporarily unavailable or overloaded
is the right code for planned maintenance, often with a Retry-After header
cards.use: need to tell clients and crawlers to come back later during maintenance
not: means the proxy could not parse the backend's reply

cards.subject: A 504 response
says: means the proxy gave up waiting for the backend
points to a slow backend or a proxy timeout that is too short
cards.use: see a proxy return an error only after a long pause
not: means the backend crashed and refused the connection at once

cards.subject: TLS
says: encrypts traffic between client and server
lets the client verify the server's identity
replaced the obsolete SSL protocols
cards.use: need to protect data in transit across the internet
not: encrypts the data stored on the server's disk

cards.subject: A TLS certificate
says: binds a public key to a domain name
is signed by a certificate authority
has an expiry date
cards.use: need browsers to trust that a server is who it claims to be
not: contains the private key that visitors download to decrypt traffic

cards.subject: A certificate authority
says: signs certificates to vouch for an identity
is trusted because its root sits in the browser and operating system trust stores
cards.use: need to know who vouches for a certificate
not: stores copies of every site's private key

cards.subject: Let's Encrypt
says: is a free certificate authority
issues certificates through the automated ACME protocol
cards.use: want free certificates that renew without manual steps
not: sells only certificates that need paperwork about the company

cards.subject: Certbot
says: is an ACME client that obtains and renews certificates
can create the HTTPS virtual host in Apache for you
renews certificates from a scheduled timer
cards.use: need to get a Let's Encrypt certificate onto an Apache server
not: is the authority that signs the certificate

cards.subject: A certificate chain
says: links the server certificate to a trusted root through intermediates
breaks some clients when an intermediate is not served
cards.use: see a site trusted in a browser but failing in curl or an older client
not: is the list of every site that shares a certificate

cards.subject: SNI
says: lets the client name the host it wants during the TLS handshake
allows one IP address to serve several certificates
cards.use: need several HTTPS sites on one IP address
not: is needed only for sites that use a wildcard certificate

cards.subject: HSTS
says: is a response header telling browsers to use only HTTPS for a domain for a set time
makes browsers refuse to click through certificate errors on that domain
cards.use: want browsers to refuse plain HTTP to your domain
not: redirects HTTP to HTTPS on the server side

cards.subject: Cloudflare's Full (strict) mode
says: encrypts the Cloudflare-to-origin leg and validates the origin certificate
rejects an origin certificate that is expired or issued for the wrong name
cards.use: want the whole path from visitor to origin encrypted and verified
not: sends traffic to the origin as plain HTTP

cards.subject: Cloudflare's Flexible mode
says: encrypts only the visitor-to-Cloudflare leg
sends traffic to the origin as plain HTTP
can cause redirect loops when the origin forces HTTPS
cards.use: have an origin that cannot serve HTTPS at all, accepting an unencrypted last hop
not: validates the origin certificate before connecting

cards.subject: Mutual TLS
says: makes the client present a certificate as well as the server
authenticates machines to each other without passwords
cards.use: need a service to prove which client is calling it
not: is the default for ordinary browser visits to websites

cards.subject: An A record
says: maps a hostname to an IPv4 address
is what a browser needs to find the server for a name
cards.use: need a domain name to reach a server's IPv4 address
not: maps a hostname to another hostname

cards.subject: A CNAME record
says: makes one name an alias of another name
cannot share a name with other record types
cannot sit at the zone apex under standard DNS
cards.use: want www to follow whatever the main name points to
not: maps a name straight to an IP address

cards.subject: An MX record
says: names the mail servers for a domain
carries a priority number where the lowest is tried first
cards.use: need email for a domain to arrive at a particular provider
not: lists which hosts may send mail for the domain

cards.subject: A TXT record
says: holds free-form text
is where SPF policies and domain-ownership tokens are published
cards.use: need to prove to a provider that you control a domain
not: maps a hostname to an IP address

cards.subject: A DNS TTL
says: says how long resolvers may cache an answer
is best lowered ahead of a planned IP change
cards.use: plan to move a site to a new IP and want the change to spread fast
not: is the time a nameserver takes to answer one query

cards.subject: An NS record
says: delegates a zone to its authoritative nameservers
is what the registrar publishes to point the world at your DNS provider
cards.use: need to change which provider answers DNS for a domain
not: names the mail servers for a domain

cards.subject: An SPF record
says: lists the servers allowed to send mail for a domain
is published as a TXT record
checks the envelope sender, not the visible From address
cards.use: need to say which servers may send your domain's email
not: signs each message with a private key

cards.subject: A DKIM signature
says: signs each outgoing message with a private key
publishes the verifying public key in DNS under a selector
survives forwarding if the signed parts are not modified
cards.use: want receivers to verify that a message was not altered in transit
not: lists the IP addresses allowed to send mail

cards.subject: A DMARC policy
says: tells receivers what to do when a message fails SPF and DKIM alignment with the From domain
can send aggregate reports to an address
offers the policies none, quarantine and reject
cards.use: want to see who sends mail in your domain's name and block spoofing
not: signs messages with a private key

cards.subject: A PTR record
says: maps an IP address back to a hostname
is controlled by whoever owns the IP, usually the hosting provider
is often checked by receiving mail servers against the name the sender announces
cards.use: see mail rejected because the sending IP has no reverse name
not: maps a hostname to an IPv4 address

cards.subject: A firewall
says: allows or blocks traffic by address, port and protocol
works best with a default-deny stance for inbound traffic
cards.use: need to close every port the server does not need
not: encrypts traffic between the server and visitors

cards.subject: The ufw tool
says: is a simplified front end for Linux firewall rules
takes commands such as ufw allow 22/tcp
cards.use: want a simple way to set firewall rules on Ubuntu
not: obtains and renews certificates

cards.subject: SSH key authentication
says: proves identity with a private key whose public half is in authorized_keys
never sends the private key to the server
cards.use: want logins that cannot be guessed like a password
not: sends the private key to the server at login

cards.subject: Disabling SSH password login
says: is done by setting PasswordAuthentication no
removes online password guessing as an attack path
can lock you out if no working key is installed first
cards.use: have confirmed key login works and want to end password guessing
not: also blocks key-based logins

cards.subject: The fail2ban tool
says: watches logs for repeated failures
temporarily bans offending addresses through firewall rules
cards.use: see thousands of failed logins from a few addresses
not: encrypts the SSH connection

cards.subject: SSH port forwarding
says: tunnels a local port to a remote service through the SSH connection
lets a laptop reach a database bound to the server's loopback address
cards.use: need to query a database that listens only on 127.0.0.1 on the server
not: opens the remote port to the whole internet

cards.subject: A service bound to 127.0.0.1
says: accepts connections only from the same machine
is unreachable from other hosts even with no firewall
cards.use: want an app reachable only through the local proxy
not: listens on every network interface

cards.subject: A service bound to 0.0.0.0
says: listens on every network interface
is reachable from outside unless a firewall blocks it
cards.use: need to understand why a database is visible from the internet
not: accepts connections only from the same machine

cards.subject: A bastion host
says: is one hardened host that is the only way into a private network
centralises and logs administrative access
cards.use: want one audited entry point to servers with no public addresses
not: stores the off-site backups

cards.subject: The systemd service manager
says: is the init system and service manager on most Linux distributions
starts services in dependency order at boot
is controlled with systemctl
cards.use: want a service to start at boot and restart if it dies
not: is a Node.js-specific process manager

cards.subject: A systemd unit file
says: declares how a service starts through ExecStart
can set the user, environment and restart policy
needs systemctl daemon-reload after it is edited
cards.use: need to run your own app as a system service
not: is read by PM2 to start Node apps

cards.subject: PM2
says: is a process manager for Node.js apps
restarts an app that crashes
lists its apps with pm2 list
cards.use: need to keep a Node app running and restart it on a crash
not: is Linux's own init system

cards.subject: The pm2 save command
says: writes the current process list to disk so it can be restored
only restores apps after a reboot when a startup hook is also set up
cards.use: need PM2 apps to come back after a reboot
not: starts every saved app immediately

cards.subject: A PM2 ecosystem file
says: describes apps, scripts, environment and instance counts in one config
is passed to pm2 start or startOrRestart
cards.use: want PM2 app settings kept in one file in the repository
not: declares ExecStart for systemd

cards.subject: A graceful reload
says: starts new workers before old ones stop so requests are not dropped
lets in-flight requests finish
cards.use: need to deploy with no visible downtime
not: kills the process immediately

cards.subject: PM2 cluster mode
says: runs several copies of a Node app sharing one port
uses more than one CPU core
cards.use: need a single-threaded Node app to use all cores
not: splits one request across several servers

cards.subject: The SIGTERM signal
says: asks a process to shut down cleanly
can be caught so the app finishes its work first
cards.use: need a service to stop without losing in-flight work
not: cannot be caught or ignored

cards.subject: The SIGKILL signal
says: ends a process immediately
cannot be caught or ignored
cards.use: need to end a process that ignores polite stop requests
not: lets the app finish its shutdown handlers first

cards.subject: A container
says: is an isolated process that shares the host's kernel
starts quickly because it carries no guest operating system
cards.use: need to package an app with its dependencies so it runs the same anywhere
not: includes its own full operating system kernel

cards.subject: A Docker image
says: is a read-only template that containers start from
is built in stacked layers
cards.use: need a reproducible package to deploy
not: is a running instance of an app

cards.subject: A Dockerfile
says: is a text recipe of build steps for an image
starts from a base image with FROM
cards.use: need to describe how to build an app image
not: stores a container's runtime data

cards.subject: A Docker volume
says: stores data outside the container's writable layer
survives the container being removed
cards.use: need a database's data to outlive container replacement
not: is a backup of the data it holds

cards.subject: A bind mount
says: maps a specific host directory into the container
depends on the host path existing and having the right permissions
cards.use: need a container to read config files from a host folder
not: is managed entirely by Docker under its own storage area

cards.subject: A published port
says: maps a host port to a container port
is set with -p, as in 127.0.0.1:5432:5432
cards.use: need a container's service reachable from the host
not: is reachable only from inside the container's own network

cards.subject: Docker layer caching
says: reuses unchanged build steps from earlier builds
invalidates a step and every later one when its inputs change
rewards copying dependency manifests before source code
cards.use: want faster image rebuilds when only source code changed
not: rebuilds every layer on every build

cards.subject: A container healthcheck
says: runs a command on a schedule to mark the container healthy or unhealthy
is declared with HEALTHCHECK in a Dockerfile
cards.use: need Docker to know whether the app inside works, not merely runs
not: publishes the container port on the host

cards.subject: A non-root container user
says: limits the damage if the app inside is compromised
is set with the USER instruction
cards.use: want to harden an image against a compromised app
not: is required before a container can start

cards.subject: Shared hosting
says: puts many customers' sites on one server
gives no root access
can slow your site when neighbours use many resources
cards.use: need the cheapest way to run a small site with no admin work
not: gives you a dedicated virtual machine with root

cards.subject: A VPS
says: is a virtual machine slice of a physical host with root access
leaves OS patching and security to you
cards.use: need root access and custom software for a modest site
not: gives no root access and locks the software stack

cards.subject: A platform as a service
says: runs your code while the provider manages the OS and scaling
trades control for less operational work
cards.use: want to deploy code without patching or managing servers
not: hands you a bare machine to configure from scratch

cards.subject: A serverless function
says: runs code per event and is billed by execution
can suffer a cold-start delay on a first call
has no server for you to patch
cards.use: have spiky, occasional work and want to pay only when code runs
not: keeps a process running continuously between requests

cards.subject: Vertical scaling
says: adds CPU or memory to a single machine
hits a ceiling at the largest machine available
cards.use: need a quick fix for one overloaded server
not: adds more machines behind a load balancer

cards.subject: Horizontal scaling
says: adds more machines behind a load balancer
needs the app to be stateless or to share its state
cards.use: need to grow capacity beyond what one machine can offer
not: upgrades the CPU of one machine

cards.subject: A single point of failure
says: is one component whose failure takes the whole service down
is removed by adding redundancy
cards.use: want to find what one failure could take offline
not: is a server with the most traffic

cards.subject: A stateless app server
says: keeps no user session data in its own memory or disk
can be replaced or duplicated without losing user state
cards.use: want any instance to be able to serve any request
not: stores each user's session in local memory

cards.subject: Right-sizing
says: matches instance size to measured usage
cuts cost without cutting capacity that is used
cards.use: see servers running at a small fraction of capacity for months
not: buys the largest instance to avoid ever scaling

cards.subject: Egress charges
says: bill for data leaving a provider's network
grow with downloads, replication and off-provider backups
cards.use: see a data-transfer line growing on the cloud bill
not: bill for data entering the provider's network

cards.subject: The 3-2-1 rule
says: calls for three copies, two kinds of storage and one copy off-site
is a rule of thumb for how many copies to keep and where
cards.use: need a quick test of whether a backup plan is sound
not: calls for one copy kept on the same disk as the data

cards.subject: An incremental backup
says: copies only data changed since the previous backup
needs the chain back to the last full backup to restore
cards.use: want small, fast nightly backups
not: copies everything on every run

cards.subject: RPO
says: is the maximum data loss, measured in time, that is acceptable
sets how often backups must run
cards.use: need to decide how often to back up
not: is the maximum acceptable time to restore service

cards.subject: RTO
says: is the maximum acceptable time to get service back
drives the choice of restore method
cards.use: need to state how long an outage can last
not: is the maximum data loss measured in time

cards.subject: A restore test
says: restores a backup into a scratch environment to prove it works
finds missing files or bad credentials before an emergency
cards.use: want evidence that a backup is usable
not: checks only that the backup file exists

cards.subject: The pg_dump tool
says: makes a logical backup of one PostgreSQL database
can write a compressed file
is restored with psql or pg_restore depending on format
cards.use: need a consistent backup of a PostgreSQL database while it runs
not: copies the raw data directory file by file

cards.subject: The sqlite3 .backup command
says: makes a consistent copy of a SQLite database that is in use
avoids the torn copy a plain file copy can produce
cards.use: need a safe backup of a live SQLite file
not: can only be used after the app is stopped

cards.subject: A disk snapshot
says: captures a volume at a point in time
is fast to take
often lives with the same provider and account as the disk
cards.use: need a quick rollback point before a risky change
not: counts as the off-site copy by itself

cards.subject: An immutable backup
says: cannot be changed or deleted until its retention period ends
protects backups from ransomware or a compromised admin account
cards.use: worry that an attacker with admin access could delete the backups
not: is rewritten every night to stay current

cards.subject: Uptime monitoring
says: probes a site from outside on a schedule
alerts when requests fail
cards.use: need to hear about an outage before customers do
not: measures CPU use inside the server only

cards.subject: A health check endpoint
says: returns success when the app can serve requests
is polled by monitors and load balancers
cards.use: need a URL that says whether the app is up
not: lists the app's users

cards.subject: A liveness check
says: asks whether a process is stuck and should be restarted
triggers a restart when it fails
cards.use: need stuck processes restarted automatically
not: removes the instance from rotation without restarting it

cards.subject: A readiness check
says: asks whether an instance is ready to receive traffic
removes the instance from rotation without restarting it when it fails
cards.use: need traffic held back while an app warms up or loses its database
not: restarts the process when it fails

cards.subject: The four golden signals
says: are latency, traffic, errors and saturation
give a compact view of service health
cards.use: need a starter set of metrics for any service
not: are CPU, RAM, disk and network totals only

cards.subject: Alert fatigue
says: happens when noisy alerts teach people to ignore them
is reduced by alerting only on actionable problems
cards.use: see on-call staff muting pages
not: is caused by having too few alerts

cards.subject: p99 latency
says: is the time that 99 percent of requests beat
exposes slow outliers that an average hides
cards.use: need to see how bad the slowest requests are
not: is the average response time

cards.subject: A service level objective
says: is a target for reliability, such as a share of successful requests over a period
defines an error budget of allowed failure
cards.use: need to decide how much unreliability is acceptable before work shifts to stability
not: is a contract with penalty payments

cards.subject: A symptom-based alert
says: fires on user-visible problems such as error rate
avoids paging on causes that may do no harm
cards.use: want pages that mean users are hurt, not that CPU was high for a minute
not: fires whenever any resource crosses a threshold

cards.subject: A CDN
says: caches content on servers close to users
reduces load on the origin
speeds up static files for distant visitors
cards.use: need images and scripts to load faster for visitors worldwide
not: replaces the origin's database

cards.subject: The Cache-Control header
says: tells caches how long a response may be stored
uses directives such as max-age and no-store
cards.use: need to say how long a response may be reused
not: lists the hosts allowed to call the API

cards.subject: A cache purge
says: removes cached copies from the edge before they expire
is how a changed file reaches visitors at once
cards.use: have just fixed a file but visitors still get the old one
not: extends how long old copies are kept

cards.subject: A load balancer
says: spreads requests across several backends
stops sending traffic to backends that fail health checks
cards.use: need more than one server to share traffic
not: caches static files at locations near visitors

cards.subject: The round-robin method
says: gives each backend a turn in order
ignores how busy each backend is
cards.use: want the simplest way to spread requests evenly
not: sends each request to the backend with the fewest active connections

cards.subject: The least-connections method
says: sends each request to the backend with the fewest active connections
suits requests that take very different times
cards.use: have requests of very uneven length
not: gives each backend a turn regardless of load

cards.subject: A sticky session
says: pins a client to the same backend across requests
is a workaround for apps that keep session state in server memory
cards.use: have an app that cannot share session state between servers
not: lets any backend serve any request equally

cards.subject: The X-Forwarded-For header
says: carries the original client address through proxies
can be forged by clients unless the first trusted proxy sets it
cards.use: need the real visitor IP behind a proxy
not: encrypts the client address

cards.subject: Rate limiting
says: caps requests per client in a time window
typically answers excess requests with 429
cards.use: need to blunt scraping or password guessing
not: speeds up responses by caching them

cards.subject: An exposed origin IP
says: lets attackers bypass the CDN's protection by hitting the server directly
is mitigated by accepting traffic only from the CDN's address ranges
cards.use: worry that the CDN's protection can be skipped
not: is harmless when the CDN is enabled

cards.subject: A proxied DNS record
says: answers with the CDN's addresses instead of the origin's
keeps the origin address out of ordinary lookups
cards.use: want visitors to reach the CDN rather than the origin
not: points the name straight at the origin's IP

cards.subject: The deploy script's rsync step
says: copies the project to the server directory with --delete
excludes node_modules, build output, git data, database files and env files
keeps server-only data and secrets from being wiped
cards.use: need to explain why a deploy cannot erase the production database
not: overwrites the SQLite database with the developer's copy

cards.subject: The deploy script's flock lock
says: stops two deploys running on the server at once
fails the second deploy immediately with a message instead of waiting
cards.use: worry about two overlapping deploys
not: limits how many visitors can use the site

cards.subject: The deploy script's npm ci step
says: installs exactly what the lockfile specifies
fails when the lockfile and package.json disagree
cards.use: need a repeatable clean install on the server
not: upgrades packages to the newest versions allowed

cards.subject: The schema push without --force
says: lets drizzle-kit stop when a change would delete rows
makes the deploy fail rather than silently run a delete
cards.use: want a risky schema change to halt the deploy
not: forces every change through even when data would be lost

cards.subject: The deploy script's health loop
says: polls the local app port up to ten times, three seconds apart
succeeds only when it sees HTTP 200
prints the recent PM2 error logs when it gives up
cards.use: need proof the new version is serving before calling the deploy done
not: waits a fixed minute and assumes success

cards.subject: The PM2 restart step in the deploy
says: runs pm2 startOrRestart with the ecosystem file
starts the app if it is not running and restarts it if it is
is followed by pm2 save
cards.use: need the deploy to bring the new build live under PM2
not: deletes the app from PM2 and recreates it by hand

cards.subject: The ssh bash -s pattern
says: pipes the remote steps into bash on the server
keeps the fish login shell from parsing bash syntax
cards.use: need bash-only syntax to run on a server whose login shell is fish
not: makes ssh transfer files faster

cards.subject: The Cloudflare-only allow-list
says: is an Apache file of Require ip lines for Cloudflare's ranges plus loopback
refuses requests that reach the origin from any other address
stops the client address taken from X-Forwarded-For being spoofed by bypassing Cloudflare
cards.use: need to stop visitors bypassing Cloudflare to hit the origin directly
not: lets any address reach the app directly
like: The plain Include of the allow-list

cards.subject: The plain Include of the allow-list
says: is used instead of IncludeOptional on purpose
makes Apache refuse to load its config if the file is missing
cards.use: want a missing security file to be a loud failure rather than silent exposure
not: quietly skips the file when it is absent

cards.subject: The update-cloudflare-ips script
says: regenerates the allow-list from Cloudflare's published IPv4 and IPv6 ranges
refuses to write a list that looks too short
writes to a temporary file and moves it into place
cards.use: need to refresh the allow-list when Cloudflare's ranges change
not: reloads Apache on the server by itself

cards.subject: The certbot-created 443 vhost
says: is a copy of the port 80 virtual host made on the server
needs the same allow-list Include line as the port 80 one
cards.use: worry that the HTTPS vhost has lost a protection added to the HTTP one
not: inherits every later change to the port 80 file automatically

cards.subject: The sites-enabled copy trap
says: happens when the live file is a regular copy rather than a symlink
lets edits in sites-available pass configtest and reload yet change nothing
is found with apachectl -S
cards.use: see an Apache change that has no effect after a clean reload
not: is fixed by restarting the database

cards.subject: AllowOverride All on GG Money
says: lets Apache honour the .htaccess file for that site
is needed because its security rules live in .htaccess
avoids exposing source and config for download
cards.use: need to know why one site's virtual host needs an override that others do not
not: is set so that visitors can edit the rules

cards.subject: The Node version mismatch trap
says: came from a login bash loading nvm and putting Node 18 first
ran against PM2 using Node 20 from /usr/bin
is avoided by putting /usr/bin first in the deploy
cards.use: see install, build and runtime disagree on the Node version
not: came from PHP-FPM using the wrong pool

cards.subject: The failed-build trap
says: deleted the build directory before the build failed
left the running site without its files
is fixed by building into a fresh directory and swapping it in on success
cards.use: need to avoid a failed build taking the live site down
not: was caused by the lockfile being too new

cards.subject: GG Social's database container
says: runs PostgreSQL in Docker, published only on 127.0.0.1
keeps its data in a named volume so it survives container replacement
is copied to a backups folder before a schema push
cards.use: need to explain how the database is kept private yet persistent
not: is exposed on a public port so the app can reach it

cards.subject: The Mac lockfile trap
says: came from a lockfile made on a Mac skipping the Linux build of a native Tailwind dependency
made the server build fail until the dependency was installed explicitly without saving
cards.use: see a build pass on a laptop but die on the Linux server
not: came from the server running out of inodes

cards.subject: The GGLearn app listener
says: listens only on 127.0.0.1, port 3400
is reached by the public only through Apache
cards.use: wonder why the app port cannot be hit directly from the internet
not: is published on a public interface for Cloudflare to reach

cards.subject: ProxyPreserveHost in the GGLearn vhost
says: keeps the public hostname in the Host header the app sees
matters because Next compares the Origin with the Host on server actions
cards.use: need server actions to pass their Origin check behind the proxy
not: rewrites the Origin header to the app's local address

qa.q: Which command shows free and used disk space for each filesystem in human-readable units?
qa.right: df -h
qa.why: df reports filesystem usage; free reports memory.

qa.q: Which TCP port does HTTPS use by default?
qa.why: HTTP is 80, SSH is 22; 443 is the HTTPS default.

qa.q: Which TCP port does SSH use by default?
qa.why: 21 is FTP, 23 is Telnet and 25 is SMTP.

qa.q: What does this command do?
qa.right: It lets only the owner read and write the file
wrong: It makes the file executable by everyone
It lets everyone read it but only the owner write
It removes all access, including the owner's
qa.why: 600 means read and write for the owner and nothing for group or others.

qa.q: Given this listing, who can read the file?
qa.right: The owner and members of the group, but not other users
qa.why: The mode rw-r----- gives the owner read-write, the group read-only and others nothing.

qa.q: What does this command do?
qa.right: Creates a symbolic link so the site config is enabled without copying it
wrong: Copies the file, so later edits to the original are not seen
Reloads Apache with the new site
qa.why: A symlink points at the original, so edits to one are seen through the other.

qa.q: When does this cron entry run?
qa.right: Every day at 02:30
wrong: Every 2 hours on the 30th of the month
At 30 seconds past 2 o'clock every day
qa.why: The fields are minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week.

qa.q: When does this cron entry run?
qa.right: At 03:00 every Sunday
wrong: At 03:00 on the third of each month
qa.why: Day-of-week 0 is Sunday, with minute 0 and hour 3.

qa.q: What does this command show?
qa.right: Which process is listening on TCP port 3400
wrong: It kills every process using port 3400
The HTTP response time of port 3400
qa.why: ss -ltnp lists listening TCP sockets numerically with their processes.

qa.q: What does the -I option do here?
qa.right: Fetches only the response headers
wrong: Sends the request through a proxy
Downloads the body to a file
qa.why: curl -I sends a HEAD request and prints the headers.

qa.q: What does this command print?
qa.right: Only the HTTP status code of the response
qa.why: -o /dev/null discards the body and -w prints the chosen variable.

qa.q: What does this command show?
qa.right: Logs of the nginx unit from the last hour
wrong: The access log lines of every site for an hour
All system logs older than an hour
The users who ran nginx in the last hour
qa.why: -u picks the unit and --since limits the time range.

qa.q: What is the safe order for changing an Apache configuration?
qa.right: Edit, run apachectl configtest, then reload
wrong: Edit, restart, then read the logs
Reload first so Apache validates the new file
qa.why: A failed test stops a typo from taking every site down.

qa.q: What does --delete do in this command?
qa.right: Removes files in the destination that are not in the source
wrong: Deletes the source files after copying
Deletes destination files older than a day
Deletes the local copy after a successful transfer
qa.why: It makes the destination mirror the source, which is why server-only data must be excluded.

qa.q: A remote server's firewall is default-deny for inbound traffic and has no rule for port 22. What is the likely effect on your next SSH login?
qa.right: New SSH connections are refused and you can be locked out
wrong: SSH works because it is encrypted
SSH works because it is the default port
qa.why: A default-deny firewall drops anything not explicitly allowed.

qa.q: A site loads in desktop browsers but an API client fails with an unknown-issuer error. What is the most likely cause?
qa.right: The server does not send the intermediate certificate
wrong: DNS points to the wrong IP
qa.why: Browsers can fetch missing intermediates; many clients cannot, so a chain gap fails there only.

qa.q: Browsers show a full-page certificate warning on a site that worked yesterday, and auto-renewal was set up. What should you check first?
qa.right: The certificate's expiry date and the renewal timer's logs
qa.why: A silently failing renewal is the usual cause of a sudden expiry.

qa.q: Users get 502 Bad Gateway from the Apache proxy right after a deploy. What do you check first?
qa.right: Whether the app process is running and answering on its local port
qa.why: A 502 means the proxy could not get a valid reply from the backend.

qa.q: Disk usage reads 100 percent but du on / adds up to far less. A large log file was deleted while its service ran. What explains this?
qa.right: The service still holds the deleted file open, so the space is not freed until it closes or restarts
wrong: Deleted files move to a hidden trash on the same disk
qa.why: Space is released only when the last open handle closes; lsof can show it.

qa.q: Writes fail with 'No space left on device' but df -h shows plenty of free space. What is the next check?
qa.right: Inode usage with df -i
qa.why: Millions of tiny files can exhaust inodes before blocks.

qa.q: A DNS change is planned for tomorrow. What should you do today to make the cutover faster?
qa.right: Lower the record's TTL so caches expire sooner
wrong: Raise the TTL so more resolvers keep the record
qa.why: Caches keep the old answer for the TTL that was in effect when they fetched it.

qa.q: Outbound email from a new server lands in spam. SPF passes. What else should you check?
qa.right: DKIM signing, DMARC alignment and matching reverse DNS for the sending IP
wrong: A CNAME for the main domain
The speed of the DNS provider
qa.why: Receivers weigh several signals beyond SPF.

qa.q: A team sets Cloudflare to Flexible because the origin forces HTTPS, and the site now loops with too many redirects. What is the best fix?
qa.right: Install a valid certificate on the origin and use Full (strict)
wrong: Add a second redirect at the origin
qa.why: Flexible talks to the origin over HTTP, which the origin keeps redirecting to HTTPS.

qa.q: A database container is started with -p 5432:5432 on a host where ufw denies inbound traffic, yet a scan reaches port 5432. Why?
qa.right: Docker adds its own firewall rules that bypass ufw for published ports
wrong: Published ports are only reachable from the local machine
qa.why: Binding the publish to 127.0.0.1 avoids the exposure.

qa.q: Your only backup is a nightly copy to another folder on the same disk. The disk fails. What does this show?
qa.right: It was not a real backup because it shared the failure with the original
wrong: The copy should have been compressed
The job should have run hourly
The data is safe in the copy
qa.why: A backup must survive the failure it protects against.

qa.q: A backup job has shown green every night for a year and the database server is now lost. What is the biggest risk?
qa.right: The backups have never been restored, so they may be unusable
wrong: Compression made the files too small
A green status proves a restore will work
qa.why: Only a restore test proves a backup works.

qa.q: What is the danger of copying a live SQLite database with cp while the app writes to it?
qa.right: The copy can be torn or inconsistent
wrong: The copy always loses its indexes only
qa.why: Use the sqlite3 .backup command for a consistent copy.

qa.q: A Node app crashes at 3 a.m. and stays down until morning. What is the fix?
qa.right: Run it under a process manager such as systemd or PM2 with a restart policy
wrong: Restart it from a cron job every morning
qa.why: A process manager restarts a crashed app automatically.

qa.q: Why does a restart policy with backoff matter for a service that crashes at start?
qa.right: It avoids a tight crash loop that hammers the machine and floods the logs
wrong: It removes the need to read logs
It stops the disk filling with images
qa.why: Backoff spaces retries so a persistent fault does not consume the host.

qa.q: Why is this Dockerfile order slow for rebuilds?
qa.right: Any source change invalidates the cache before npm ci, so dependencies reinstall every build
wrong: npm ci cannot run after COPY
COPY . . deletes node_modules in the image
qa.why: Copying the lockfile and installing first lets the install layer stay cached.

qa.q: What does this command list?
qa.right: The running containers
qa.why: docker ps lists running containers; -a adds stopped ones.

qa.q: What does the -p part of this command do?
qa.right: Publishes the port on the host's loopback only, so only the host can connect
wrong: Opens the port to the internet
Limits the container to one CPU
qa.why: Prefixing the host side with 127.0.0.1 restricts who can reach it.

qa.q: What does the -v part of this command do?
qa.right: Mounts a named volume so the data survives removing the container
wrong: Copies the database to a remote backup
qa.why: A named volume lives outside the container's writable layer.

qa.q: Which of these is horizontal scaling?
qa.right: Adding a second server behind a load balancer
qa.why: Horizontal scaling adds machines rather than enlarging one.

qa.q: You add a second app server behind a load balancer and users are randomly logged out. Sessions are kept in each server's memory. What is the best long-term fix?
qa.right: Move session state to a shared store or signed cookies so any server can handle any request
qa.why: Stateless servers make horizontal scaling work.

qa.q: A monitor checks only that port 443 accepts connections, but the app crashed behind a working proxy. What is a better check?
qa.right: An HTTP request to a health endpoint that expects a 200 from the app
wrong: Reading the CPU once an hour
qa.why: A connection check proves the proxy is up, not the app.

qa.q: Average response time looks fine but customers complain of slowness. Which metric should you look at?
qa.right: A high percentile such as p99 latency
qa.why: Averages hide the slow tail that some users experience.

qa.q: What does the first line of this script do?
qa.right: Stops at the first error, treats unset variables as errors and fails a pipeline if any stage fails
wrong: Prints each command before it runs
Runs the script in the background
qa.why: These options make a script fail loudly instead of continuing in a bad state.

qa.q: If another deploy holds the lock, what does the second line do?
qa.right: Exits immediately instead of waiting
wrong: Waits until the other deploy finishes
qa.why: flock -n is non-blocking and fails at once when the lock is taken.

qa.q: A teammate edited sites-available but nothing changed after a reload. Which command do you run first?
qa.right: apachectl -S
qa.why: It shows which config file each virtual host is really loaded from.

qa.q: The allow-list file is loaded with a plain Include and is accidentally missing on a server. What happens?
qa.right: Apache refuses to load its configuration, which is the intended loud failure
wrong: Apache starts and silently serves everyone
qa.why: IncludeOptional would have skipped the file silently.

qa.q: A deploy step uses $(date) and, run through a fish login shell, silently produces nothing. What is the cure?
qa.right: Stream the commands into bash with ssh host bash -s
wrong: Switch Apache to the prefork MPM
qa.why: Fish cannot parse bash command substitution, so bash must parse the steps.

qa.q: A build step deletes the old build directory first and then fails, leaving visitors with errors. What redesign prevents this?
qa.right: Build into a fresh directory and swap it in only when the build succeeds
wrong: Delete the directory after the restart
qa.why: The old version should keep serving until the new one is proven.

qa.q: What does this command do?
qa.right: Tests the Nginx configuration for syntax errors without applying it
wrong: Starts Nginx in test mode with sample traffic
qa.why: nginx -t validates the config file.

qa.q: What does the proxy_set_header line do?
qa.right: Passes the requested hostname to the backend instead of the backend's address
wrong: Redirects visitors to the host's IP
Caches the host name for an hour
qa.why: It is the Nginx counterpart of Apache's ProxyPreserveHost.

qa.q: What does this command return?
qa.right: The mail servers for example.com
qa.why: MX records name a domain's mail servers.

qa.q: What does -all at the end of this SPF record mean?
qa.right: Mail from servers not listed should fail SPF
wrong: Mail from unlisted servers is only marked suspicious
qa.why: -all is a hard fail while ~all is a soft fail.

qa.q: Which redirect code do you use when moving a site permanently from http to https?
qa.why: 301 signals a permanent move; 302 is temporary.

qa.q: A load balancer keeps sending traffic to a crashed backend for half a minute before noticing. What reduces this?
qa.right: A shorter health check interval and a lower failure threshold
qa.why: Faster detection removes the dead backend from rotation sooner.

qa.q: Your origin is behind Cloudflare, but anyone who learns its IP can hit it directly and set a fake X-Forwarded-For. What is the best control?
qa.right: Accept traffic only from the CDN's published IP ranges at the origin
wrong: Rename the server to hide it
qa.why: If only the CDN can connect, the header it sets can be trusted.

qa.q: What does Restart=on-failure do in this unit file?
qa.right: Restarts the service after an unclean exit such as a crash
wrong: Restarts after every clean exit too
Reloads config when a file changes
qa.why: on-failure restarts on error exits, signals and timeouts, not on a clean stop.

qa.q: After a reboot a server's PM2 apps are gone. What was missing?
qa.right: A startup hook (pm2 startup) together with pm2 save of the process list
qa.why: The saved list is restored only if PM2 itself starts at boot.

qa.q: A deploy fails safely because drizzle-kit push would delete rows after you added a NOT NULL column with no default to a table that has data. Should you add --force?
qa.right: No; make the change safe first, for example with a default or a backfill, so no rows are deleted
wrong: Yes, force is always safe in production
Yes, then restore from the CDN
qa.why: The failure is the safeguard working; force would turn it into data loss.

qa.q: Uploads fail with permission denied. The web server runs as www-data and the folder is owned by root with mode 755. What is the right fix?
qa.right: Give the web server user ownership of just the uploads folder
wrong: Run the web server as root
qa.why: Grant the narrowest access that works.
